bull.b: Affirm has moved from substantial losses to meaningful profitability while converting earnings into strong operating and free cash flow. This improves internal funding capacity, supports product investment, and provides greater resilience as the platform expands over the next several quarters.

A materially stronger underwriting architecture can expand approval rates without requiring proportionate deterioration in credit performance. That combination could improve customer access, merchant conversion, and transaction growth while reinforcing Affirm’s technology-based competitive differentiation.

Strong GMV growth and a management commitment to at least 30% FY2027 growth indicate substantial expansion potential, while predominantly fixed-rate funding provides better visibility into financing costs. Together, distribution growth and funding stability support more durable operating planning.

bear.b: Although leverage is currently low, the sharp historical variation shows that Affirm’s balance-sheet requirements and funding profile can change materially. Such volatility may constrain flexibility during weaker credit or funding conditions and makes the latest capital structure less clearly durable.

Higher provisions and slightly rising delinquencies can reduce the economic benefit of transaction growth by increasing expected credit losses. If approval expansion or new-user initiatives continue to pressure credit metrics, underwriting gains may take longer to translate into sustainable margins.

A greater mix of card-based direct-to-consumer volume may broaden distribution and repeat usage but produce less revenue per GMV than integrated merchant transactions. That structural mix effect can limit take-rate expansion, while related GAAP expenses may further moderate reported operating profitability.
